text:
I need to send a quarterly update to our investors. I'm the founder of a scheduling app for physical therapy clinics. We have 6 people.

Numbers for the quarter:
- Monthly recurring revenue is $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- We added 9 clinics and lost 4. One of the 4 was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain that paid $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system.
- We have $480,000 in the bank and lose about $44,000 a month.
- Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started.
- I didn't send updates for the last two quarters.
- Next month we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month.

Under 500 words. It goes to 11 investors.

Before I draft, a few questions. The update has two problems to handle: a flat quarter after six months of silence, and roughly 11 months of runway ($480k ÷ $44k). Investors will work out the runway number in about ten seconds, so the update has to get there first. Your answers will decide what it argues.

1. **What do you want from them?** Intros to clinic chains or reminder buyers, a bridge, help planning a raise, or nothing yet? With 11 months left, they'll assume a raise is coming, so it's better to say what you plan to do.

2. **What's the runway plan, and what can you commit to?** For example, a date to start raising, a cut you'd make if a target is missed, or the MRR you need to reach break-even. I'll only include what you'll stand behind.

3. **What's behind the reminder number?** How many clinics, over what period? And is the idea behind the standalone product that clinics using their records system's built-in scheduler, like the chain that left, can still buy your reminders? If so, the loss becomes the argument for the new product. Any early sign of demand at $150 (waitlist, pilots, verbal commitments) would help.

4. **How do you count customers?** Were the 9 added and 4 lost counted per account or per location? Why did the other 3 leave? Without the chain, MRR rose about $5,500 in the quarter. That's your best number, but only if it's accurate.

5. **Why the two missed updates, and will you commit to quarterly from now on?** One honest sentence near the top works better than skipping it.

6. **Anything else they know or will find out?** Team changes, pricing changes, a churn risk you can see coming. Also, what name should I sign it with?

1. 20 minutes on the phone with each of them, and intros to clinic chains.

2. I don't have a raise date or a break-even number worked out. What I can commit to: an update in the first week of every quarter, next one January 7. And a monthly one-page set of numbers for any investor who asks.

3. I don't know how many clinics or over what period offhand. Yes, that's the idea, clinics on a records system's built-in scheduler can still buy our reminders. 6 clinics have said they'll buy it standalone when it launches December 1.

4. I don't know whether it was per account or per location, or why the other 3 left.

5. The numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. No other reason. Yes, quarterly from now on.

6. Two other customers use the same records system as the chain that left. Together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way. Sign it Sam Patel, Cadence Scheduling.

I've written the update below. It's about 440 words.

- **Revenue apart from the big loss:** MRR stayed flat even though the chain's $5,500 a month left, so everyone else together added about $5,500. That's true however customers are counted, so I used it.
- **Runway:** $480k at $44k a month runs out around October 2027. Since you don't have a raise date yet, the update says so plainly and makes working one out the main topic for the calls.
- **The customer that left:** I used it to explain the reminders-only product. The two other customers on the same records system ($3,800 a month) are in the update, without a promise that they'll stay.
- **The no-show figures:** I didn't add a clinic count or time period, so investors may ask. It's worth checking those before the calls.

Subject: Cadence Scheduling: quarterly update, November 2026

Hi all,

This is the first update I've sent in six months. Revenue was flat and I didn't want to send bad news. That was the wrong call, and it won't happen again: you'll get an update in the first week of every quarter, starting January 7.

**The numbers**
- Monthly recurring revenue: $41,000, the same as three months ago
- Clinics: 9 added, 4 lost
- Cash: $480,000. We're losing about $44,000 a month, which gives us roughly 11 months.
- Team: 6

**What happened**
Our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain paying $5,500 a month, moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system. Apart from that one loss, the rest of the business added about $5,500 in monthly revenue. That's why we ended the quarter flat and not down.

The chain leaving exposes a real risk. Two other customers use the same records system and together pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way.

**What we're doing about it**
Our strongest result is our automatic text reminders. Clinics using them have a 7% no-show rate, compared with 13% before they started. That's nearly half of missed appointments gone. A records system's built-in scheduler doesn't replace that, so we're going to sell reminders on their own.

From December 1, reminders are available as a separate product for $150 a month. Six clinics have said they'll buy it at launch. That's $900 a month, which is small. What matters is that it opens up clinics we couldn't sell full scheduling to. It also gives us a way to keep customers like the chain even after they move their scheduling elsewhere.

**Where that leaves us**
At our current spending, our cash lasts until about October 2027. I don't have a fundraising date or a break-even number worked out yet, and I'd rather tell you that than make one up. Working both out is my priority this quarter, and it's where I'd most value your help.

**What I'm asking for**
1. **20 minutes on the phone with each of you** in the next few weeks. I'd like your view on the reminder product and on how to plan around the runway. Reply with a few times that work for you.
2. **Introductions to physical therapy clinic chains**, especially ones that schedule through their electronic records system. Those clinics are now customers we can sell to.

If you'd like a one-page set of numbers every month, reply and I'll send it to you.

Thank you for your patience, and for sticking with us.

Sam Patel
Cadence Scheduling
